readerTitle: Two businesses grew 40%. Only one made more money.
caseNote: 가상 사례 (식자재 유통업체, 세무·회계 대행사, 구독 앱) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 성장이 건강한지는 전체 매출이 아니라, 새로 더해진 매출 한 건 한 건이 확보 비용과 처리 비용을 빼고 돈을 남기는지로 판단한다.
misconception: 매출이 늘면 이익도 따라 늘고, 규모가 커지면 고정비가 분산되니 어떤 성장이든 결국 이득이다.

sources.text: 관리회계의 표준 개념 (증분 이익, 공헌이익, 고객 확보·서비스 비용)

factChecks.note: 구독 앱 계산: 월 $10 − 서버·결제 비용 $2 = $8 × 평균 6개월 = $48. 광고로 구독자 1명 확보에 $70 → 1명당 −$22.

cards.title: Two businesses grew 40% last year. Only one made more money.
body: A food-service distributor and a bookkeeping firm each grew sales by about 40%.
One owner's profit more than doubled. The other's fell by a third. Same growth on paper, opposite results. The difference was hidden in the *new* sales.

image.label: Two rising sales arrows, one profit arrow pointing down
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 나란히 선 두 가게(식자재 창고와 작은 회계 사무실). 두 가게 위 매출 화살표는 똑같이 위로 올라가지만, 창고 쪽 작은 동전 더미는 줄어들고 사무실 쪽 동전 더미는 커짐. 실제 로고나 상표는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: 50 new cafés, if delivery is free.
body: You run a food-service distributor. Your sales rep can sign 50 small cafés across town if you offer free delivery. Each orders about $300 a week, and you keep 25% after paying for the goods.
Each delivery to that side of town costs about $90 in driver time and fuel. Do you take the deal?

options.text: Yes. $780,000 in new sales a year is too big to pass up
options.feedback: Big revenue, but each $300 order leaves $75 and costs $90 to deliver. Every order loses $15, so more orders means bigger losses.

options.text: Yes. More sales will spread the warehouse rent over more volume
options.feedback: Spreading fixed costs helps only when each new sale leaves something behind. Here each order is $15 short before rent gets a cent.

options.text: Only with a minimum order or a delivery fee that covers the $90
options.feedback: You keep the growth but make each order pay its own way. You may sign fewer cafés, but every one adds profit.

cards.title: Same growth rate, opposite profit.
body: The distributor took the cafés on free delivery. Sales rose 39%.
The bookkeeping firm signed 20 new clients at its normal $1,000 a month. Sales rose 40%.
cards.callout: Profit fell 33% at one and more than doubled at the other.

cards.title: Follow one new order.
body: Now a new bookkeeping client: $1,000 a month − 12 staff hours at $45 ($540) = **$460** left every month.

cards.title: Profitable vs unprofitable growth
body: **Profitable growth** adds sales that each leave money behind after the costs to win and serve them. **Unprofitable growth** adds sales that each lose money, so the faster you grow, the more you lose.
The distributor's old customers were still profitable. That hid the problem: total profit stayed positive while every new café dragged it down.

image.label: A profit stack with a new layer below the line
image.brief: 층층이 쌓인 블록 그림. 아래쪽 "Existing customers" 블록들은 초록색으로 이익선 위에 있고, 맨 위에 새로 얹은 "New customers" 블록은 빨간색으로 이익선을 아래로 끌어내림. 단순한 인포그래픽 스타일.

cards.title: Where growth quietly loses money.
body: New sales usually turn unprofitable in one of three places:
list: **Discounts to win them:** a lower price shrinks what each sale leaves
**Cost to serve:** small orders, long distances, custom requests, extra support
**Cost to win:** commissions, ads and free trials paid before the first sale
cards.callout: Revenue shows none of these. Look at the new sales on their own.

cards.title: Some losses are worth it, for a while.
body: A new route can lose money at first and turn profitable once enough cafés sign up along it, because the same van serves more stops. Spare capacity matters too: if the van drives that way anyway, the real delivery cost is lower.
But "it will pay off at scale" needs a specific reason and the cash to wait. Without both, it's a hope, not a plan.

cards.title: Now it's a subscription app.
body: Your app charges $10 a month. Servers and payment fees cost $2 per subscriber, and the average subscriber stays six months. So each one leaves about $48.
Paid ads are bringing in lots of new users, at about $70 per subscriber. What do you do?

options.text: Double the ad budget. Growth spreads your fixed costs
options.feedback: Each subscriber costs $70 to win and leaves $48. Doubling spend doubles a $22 loss per person.

options.text: Shift spend to channels where a subscriber costs less than $48
options.feedback: You keep growing, but only with customers who add profit. Growth may slow while you find those channels.

options.text: Stop all ads until people stay longer
options.feedback: Longer stays would help, but stopping everything also cuts off any channels that already pay their way.

cards.title: Grow the sales that leave money behind.
body: Before chasing growth, check what each new sale leaves after the costs to win and serve it. If the answer is negative, growing faster only loses money faster.
**Try it today:** pick your three newest customers. For each, write the price, the cost of goods, the cost to serve and the cost to win. Which ones add profit?
